purpose: Recurring work-pattern activities mined from this machine's Claude Code session corpus, for side-by-side comparison against the Roamy corpus roster (mined 2026-08-01, 87 sessions). The comparison itself is a separate consolidation step once both rosters exist in the repo.

corpus_stats.date_range: 2026-07-11 to 2026-08-02 (recency-biased sample, all within the last ~3 weeks)
filters_applied: size >= 1,800,000 bytes (raised from the 100k baseline to land the work list in the 80-120 range; at 100k there were 822 candidates)
>= 4 real human turns (string content only; excluded tool_result blocks and turns whose text starts with '<' or '[Image')
sorted by mtime descending, took the resulting 100 (recency bias — all fell within Jul 11 - Aug 2 2026)

comparison_notes: Roamy's roster (mined 2026-08-01, tagged corpus: roamy) is not present in this repo as of this run. Every activity below is tagged corpus: "m4-mini" so it can be diffed against Roamy's roster once that file lands here -- do not merge the two into one undifferentiated list.

activities.label: Requesting self-contained handover docs with absolute paths before closing/switching a session
activities.description: Before closing a window or switching machines, David repeatedly demands a durable, committed handover artifact — one file, absolute path, paste-ready launch line — so a fresh session or collaborator can resume with no access to the current chat.

evidence.quote: give me a full handover message... with one file, absolutely path written? That's how I'd want to see it.
The system that needs your readiness document is not in your folder, so it can't understand a relative path
Handover docs must ship with a paste-ready launch line... claude --model claude-fable-5 ...
Is this committed and pushed so that she'll actually see it?

activities.label: Running a Chaperone watch-loop over another live session
activities.description: David repeatedly spins up a separate read-only 'Chaperone' session that tails another running Claude Code session's transcript on a timed loop (checked against a plan/oracle doc) and pings him only on drift, completion, or a push — rather than watching the work himself.

evidence.quote: watch kbde-swag and tell me when 358 is pushed
Chaperone tick: watching dark-factory-c2 ... Oracle: backlog/2026-07-10-darkfactory-handover.md
Just watch the conversation every 30 minutes. Place it on a loop... batch them all up
You are now watched by a read-only CHAPERONE session — an advisor to David, not your boss.
